sections.h2: Who in McDuffie County values a house and who collects the tax?
sections.html:
Three bodies share the job, and they do not overlap. The Board of Assessors, working from the Tax Assessor's Office, decides taxability, value and equalization. The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and disburses. The Board of Equalization, appointed by the Grand Jury, hears administrative appeals when the assessors will not move.

Call the assessors at 706-595-2128. Doors are open to the public weekdays from 8 am until 5 pm. By the county's own description the assessors set values and nothing else, so a billing question belongs with the Tax Commissioner. Returns are also filed with the assessors in McDuffie County, under a delegation the county describes on its general info page.

  • Value, returns, exemptions and homestead filings: Tax Assessor's Office.
  • Bills, payments, tax liens and excess funds: Tax Commissioner.
  • Millage rates: set each year by the county commissioners and the school board, not by either tax office.
  • Appeals that the assessors deny: Board of Equalization, arbitration, then Superior Court.

Public hearings on the county budget and millage rate are held at the McDuffie County Government Center, 210 Railroad Street in Thomson.

sections.h2: What makes McDuffie County different from its Augusta-area neighbors?
sections.html:
McDuffie County is a small, steady county in the Augusta metro area, west of Columbia and Richmond counties. The state created it on October 18, 1870, and named it for South Carolina governor and senator George McDuffie. Thomson, incorporated in 1854 while it still sat in Columbia County, became the seat, and Dearing is the only other incorporated place. The old Wrightsborough settlement, occupied from 1768 to 1920, is kept alive by a local historic foundation.

Water in the county drains to the Savannah River: Brier Creek takes most of the south, and the Little River sub-basin takes the north. I-20 runs through, joined by US 78, US 221 and US 278. Census figures for 2022 show $68.8 million in transportation and warehousing receipts and $89.9 million in health care and social assistance.

  • Headcount: 21,640 in July 2025, almost the same as the 2020 base of 21,628.
  • Land area: 257.37 square miles at 84 people per square mile.
  • Housing: 9,725 units, with 65.0 percent lived in by their owners at a median value of $170,200. Gross rent has a median of $792.
  • Residents: 22.3 percent are 65 or older and 19.6 percent are in poverty. The median household brings in $56,733.
  • The mean trip to work is 22.7 minutes.
  • Builders pulled 86 permits during 2025.

sections.h2: When does a McDuffie County tax bill arrive, and what does lateness cost?
sections.html:
McDuffie is one of the Georgia counties with an early calendar. Bills are mailed by September 15 and are due November 15, a month ahead of the December 20 default found elsewhere. Here is the county's own schedule and penalty wording.

Dates, interest and penalties on a McDuffie bill (source: thomson-mcduffie.gov tax pages)
EventCounty wording
MailingBy September 15
Due dateNovember 15
InterestMonthly from the 16th, at the prime rate plus 3 divided by 12
Penalty5 percent every 120 days, 20 percent maximum
Tax lien (FIFA)Placed 30 days after the bill turns delinquent and filed with the Clerk of Court
Mobile homesMailed in January, due April 1

The lien matters for a seller. It is reported on your credit and filed publicly, so a clean title search is much easier before the 30 days run out.

Partial payments are accepted if they are set up before the bill turns delinquent, with a signed agreement the Tax Commissioner approves.

sections.h2: What changed on McDuffie County bills in 2026?
sections.html:
The county's 2026 tax page announced that the separate fire fee goes away, with FLOST revenue paying for fire service in its place. The county millage rate was proposed at 7.998 mills, up from 7.809 mills in 2025, to cover the cost of fire service the fee used to pay for. The vote was set for the evening hearing on October 13, 2026, so the Tax Commissioner can tell you the rate that was adopted.

The county also said a Notice of Property Tax Increase can appear even when a typical homestead's combined bill falls, because the notice is measured against the rollback rate, shown as 6.085 mills for 2026, and ignores the fire fee. City and school taxes, 15.124 mills in the estimator, appear separately on the bill.

Homesteaded property also receives a one-time state relief credit. The Tax Commissioner's page describes it as an $18,000 reduction in assessed value that is applied automatically to homesteads filed by the deadline.

sections.h2: How does a McDuffie County owner appeal a new value?
sections.html:
An owner gets 45 days counted from the date on the notice of assessment, and an appeal that arrives late is invalid. It has to be written and filed with the Board of Assessors.

After review, the assessors either change the value or pass the file along to the Board of Equalization, where both sides present a position. Either side may go on to McDuffie County Superior Court. The county also describes arbitration as a choice in place of the Board of Equalization, which you make when you file.

  • Three grounds are allowed: taxability, uniformity and value.
  • Complaints about the tax amount are not appealable.
  • Uniformity asks whether similar properties are valued alike.
  • Superior Court is open to the owner or the assessors after a Board of Equalization ruling.

A homestead denial has its own appeal. The Board of Assessors makes the final eligibility call, and a denied applicant must be notified of the procedure.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special assessments does McDuffie County list?
sections.html:
Apply at the Board of Assessors Office from January 1 through April 1, having owned and lived in the home on January 1. The county describes a legislated regular exemption of $4,000, a $15,000 exemption at 62 and older when net income is below $15,000, and a $30,000 exemption on assessed value for school purposes at 65 and older. A separate local exemption exists for owners who are 100 percent disabled, with doctor documentation and the same income test. Once approved, an exemption continues without reapplying until the owner changes.

Land has its own programs, each tied to a ten-year covenant with the county:

  • Preferential agricultural property, taxed on 30 percent of market value in place of the usual 40.
  • Conservation use, valued at current use.
  • Environmentally sensitive property kept in its natural condition.
  • Residential transitional property in an area changing to another use.

Standing timber is taxed once, when sold or harvested, at 100 percent of fair market value. The county page also describes a deferral program for homestead owners 62 and older with income of $15,000 or less, which generally lasts until ownership changes.

sections.h2: What should a seller with an unpaid McDuffie County bill do?
sections.html:
Call the Tax Commissioner and ask for the exact balance, interest and any lien charge, then ask how the payoff will be delivered to the closing attorney. A tax that is only days past due has a very different payoff from one carrying 5 percent penalty layers and a recorded lien.

The Tax Commissioner accepts cash, checks, money orders and credit or debit cards, with fees on cards and no American Express. Owners whose land was sold at a delinquent tax sale may be owed excess funds. Claims must be in writing, with proper identification, to the Tax Commissioner's office, and the county posts a list and an application.

If the house is a mobile home, handle April 1 first, since that bill is a separate account from the land.

faqs.q: When are McDuffie County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15, with bills mailed by September 15. That is earlier than the December 20 date used in many Georgia counties. Mobile home taxes are due April 1.

faqs.q: How much time do I have to appeal in McDuffie County?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the notice of assessment, and the appeal has to be written. The county treats late appeals as invalid.

faqs.q: What penalties apply to a late McDuffie County tax bill?
faqs.a: Interest accrues monthly from the 16th, and a 5 percent penalty applies every 120 days up to 20 percent. A tax lien follows 30 days after the bill turns delinquent.

faqs.q: Did McDuffie County drop its fire fee?
faqs.a: Yes, the county says there is no separate fire fee starting in 2026, and the cost moved into the county millage rate, which was proposed at 7.998 mills. Check the adopted rate with the Tax Commissioner.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for homestead exemption in McDuffie County?
faqs.a: File with the Board of Assessors Office between January 1 and April 1. The county says the tax assessor handles and approves every exemption application.
